placements.title: An instrument counts as calibrated once it is verified against reference evidence
placements.frame: What reference evidence is this instrument's calibration checked against, and does the claim hold across the whole band it is used in?
placements.why: The position holds Quill Ashgrove's assertion and the record entry about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration, verified against the June reference plates. The 88.4 MHz figure is a fact that evidences the leaf. The subject future envelopes will keep feeding is how calibration is grounded in reference data. No existing structure holds this, so the leaf stands alone.

mints.why: The content is about calibrating an observatory instrument (the Kestrelwood spectrograph) and checking it against reference plates. This is a subject later calibration decisions are likely to return to.
